tagline: Down the mill valley beside a canal that lasted twenty years.
intro: Route 122 comes down out of Grafton and follows the Blackstone River south through Northbridge, Uxbridge and Millville toward the Rhode Island line, crossing the river twice on the way. Mill villages line the valley. Mills spread north along it from Pawtucket, and the valley counts itself the first industrialized region in the country.

Beside the river ran the Blackstone Canal, 45 miles of locks and towpath between Worcester and Providence. It opened in 1828, lost its trade to the railroad and closed in 1848. About 85 percent of it is still there, some of it under brush and trees.

moments.title: Grafton Common
moments.text: Old homes and churches stand around the common, which got its bandstand from a 1930s film crew and has rebuilt it many times since.

moments.title: Blackstone River and Canal Heritage State Park
moments.text: Canal boats tied up overnight in Uxbridge on the two-day run to Providence, and near Goat Hill a granite lock and the old towpaths are still there to find.

moments.title: Millville
moments.text: Route 122 runs along the river as the town's main street, past a well-preserved lock left from the canal.
